areas.area: Mac integration, security review and release evidence

last_completed: The encrypted container works on real hardware. The owner created an encrypted project in a scratch folder on their Mac, got the one-time recovery code screen, stored it, locked the project and reopened it with the passphrase. That is the first time any of this area has run outside the test suite, it confirms the sandbox diagnosis in 14c, and it exercises create, the recovery-code handoff, lock and reopen through the app. Four silent dead ends in the encrypted workspace were then removed, all of the same shape the owner has complained about repeatedly: a control that does nothing and says nothing. The plain-to-encrypted copy could announce 'Copy prepared' and then show nothing when an encrypted project was already open; Write encrypted checkpoint did nothing with an empty note path, and nothing again when the note had left the project; and the two saved-passphrase buttons did nothing with no project chosen. All four now say why. The remaining guards in that controller were audited and left alone: they sit behind buttons that are already disabled in the matching state. Unverified source.
current_work: Continuing on the encrypted .rdm area. Now that creation and reopen are confirmed working, the next things worth exercising are the ones that were never reachable before: writing a checkpoint, the encrypted working drafts surviving a quit and reopen, and the plain-to-encrypted copy of FOLIO TEST. The owner should keep using throwaway .rdm files, not real data, since the container's own contract still says no sensitive project belongs in it. Still open in the area: checkpoint failure paths, Mac CryptoKit parity, power-loss matrices, fuzzing, independent review and Keychain device slots. Also still unwalked: the original report's checklist items and the nine polish fixes from the earlier passes.
